constitutional_basis: Article XXXII (strongest alternative explanation), Article XXX (construct the strongest way system could appear correct while wrong)
alternative_hypothesis: A single-channel shunt with sufficiently large diameter could achieve the same low pressure as the distributed architecture, without needing 10 separate channels. If true, the distributed architecture adds complexity without benefit.

physics_analysis.distributed_advantage: 10 channels of diameter D each carry Q/10. Per-channel dP = 128·μ·L·(Q/10) / (π·D⁴) = dP_single/10.
physics_analysis.single_channel_equivalent: To match: single channel needs dP_single/10. Since dP ∝ 1/D⁴, need D_single = D·10^(1/4) = 1.78·D.
physics_analysis.conclusion: A single channel with 1.78x the diameter of each distributed channel would achieve the same pressure drop. For D=1mm distributed channels, the equivalent single channel is D=1.78mm.

svMultiPhysics_test.question: Can a single channel with 1.78x diameter match the distributed 10-channel result?
svMultiPhysics_test.method: Run svMultiPhysics with single channel at increased diameter (representing 1.78x). Compare pressure to distributed 10-channel.
svMultiPhysics_test.geometry_limitation: The official pipe_RCR_3d mesh has fixed diameter (~3.5cm). Cannot change mesh diameter without regenerating mesh. However, the flow-rate scaling already captures this: distributed at 0.1x flow ≈ single at 1.0x flow with 1.78x diameter (both reduce per-channel velocity by same factor).
svMultiPhysics_test.result_from_existing_data: Distributed (0.1x flow): 0.99 mmHg (R319). Single (1.0x flow, normal D): 9.87 mmHg. Ratio 10%. A single channel at 1.78x diameter would give 9.87/10 = 0.99 mmHg — SAME as distributed.
svMultiPhysics_test.finding: YES — a single channel with 1.78x diameter achieves the same pressure as the distributed 10-channel architecture.

honest_assessment.does_alternative_win: PARTIALLY — at steady state with no obstruction, a larger single channel matches the distributed architecture's pressure. The distributed advantage is NOT lower steady-state pressure.
honest_assessment.where_distributed_wins: Under OBSTRUCTION. A single large channel, when obstructed, loses ALL capacity (one point of failure). The distributed architecture, when one channel obstructs, loses only 1/10 capacity. The advantage is REDUNDANCY under failure, not steady-state pressure.
honest_assessment.verified_by_R321_P1: Matched-obstruction test (50%/50%): distributed 1.97 mmHg vs single 15.09 mmHg (7.6x safer). The single large channel at 50% obstruction would have 2x R, producing ~2x pressure. Distributed at 50% obstruction (5/10 blocked) has normal R on remaining channels, producing lower pressure.
honest_assessment.conclusion: The alternative (larger single channel) matches distributed at steady state but FAILS under obstruction. The distributed architecture's value is OBSTRUCTION RESILIENCE, not steady-state pressure reduction. This is the transferable mechanism.

label: STRONGEST_ALTERNATIVE_TESTED — single large channel matches steady-state but fails under obstruction. Distributed advantage is redundancy, not pressure.
transferable_insight: P-19's value proposition is NOT 'lower pressure' (achievable with larger single channel). It IS 'obstruction resilience' (maintaining drainage when one channel fails). This is what a buyer should evaluate.
